Students should explain their choices, identify errors or misconceptions, and verify the result rather than relying on memorisation alone.
subtopics.worked_example: Worked example: complete a representative strategy task, identify the key rule, clue, language feature or performance criterion, then explain and verify the result.
subtopics.pitfall: Common pitfall: confusing a related term, form, interpretation or technique with the exact requirement of the task, or skipping verification after producing an answer or performance sample.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: perform or solve an unfamiliar strategy task independently, explain the reasoning or technique, correct a plausible error, and verify the final result against the stated criteria.

subtopics.title: strategy selection
subtopics.teaching: Choose a representation or method by inspecting what the puzzle asks, what information is given, and which relationships are easiest to expose.
subtopics.worked_example: For a number puzzle with repeated clues, organize the known values in a table before calculating so hidden relationships become visible.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: calculating immediately without first identifying the structure of the puzzle.
subtopics.mastery: Explain why a chosen method makes the challenge simpler and apply it correctly.

subtopics.title: multi-step reasoning
subtopics.teaching: Break playful mathematics challenges into short linked steps and keep intermediate results visible so each deduction can be checked.
subtopics.worked_example: A three-stage sharing puzzle can be solved by finding the total first, applying the first share, then checking the remaining amount before the final share.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: carrying an unchecked intermediate result into later steps.
subtopics.mastery: Solve a multi-step challenge while showing and verifying each important deduction.

subtopics.title: error spotting
subtopics.teaching: Compare a proposed solution with the original conditions, test simple cases, and locate the first step where the reasoning stops matching the puzzle.
subtopics.worked_example: If a pattern solution predicts the next term but fails when the same rule is tested on an earlier term, revisit the assumed rule.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: changing the final answer without identifying which assumption caused the error.
subtopics.mastery: Find and explain the first incorrect step in a worked mathematics puzzle.

subtopics.title: mixed maths challenges
subtopics.teaching: Combine arithmetic, patterns, geometry, measurement, data, and logical reasoning in unfamiliar contexts rather than treating each skill as isolated.
subtopics.worked_example: A treasure-map challenge may combine coordinates, distance comparisons, shape clues, and a final arithmetic code.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: using a familiar operation just because it appears in the story instead of matching the operation to the evidence.
subtopics.mastery: Select and combine multiple mathematical ideas to solve an unfamiliar challenge.

subtopics.title: championship puzzle round
subtopics.teaching: Practice timed mixed challenges with deliberate question selection, clean working, estimation checks, and final-answer verification.
subtopics.worked_example: In a timed round, secure direct points first, mark a harder puzzle, then return with the remaining time and verify every selected answer.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: spending too long on one puzzle and losing easy marks elsewhere.
subtopics.mastery: Complete a mixed challenge accurately under time pressure and justify the final answers.
